key_insight: Biased-noise qubits can drastically reduce fault-tolerance overhead only when the hardware operations preserve the error hierarchy, so phase-flips and bit-flips are handled differently by design.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware teams, the paper shows that a bias-preserving CX gate or an equivalent high-fidelity multi-qubit Z readout can turn biased physical noise into a practical advantage for error correction and magic-state preparation.
method: Classify fault-tolerant protocols by the available bias-preserving operations (CZ only vs CX available).
Use dedicated codes for frequent phase-flips and concatenate with high-rate codes for rare bit-flips.
Replace CX with measurement-based architectures using non-demolition Pauli-Z syndrome extraction when needed.
evidence_signal: The review argues from experimentally relevant error rates that CZ-only syndrome gadgets can erase the benefit of noise bias, while CX-enabled or measurement-based schemes recover substantial overhead reductions.
watch_item: The main limitation is hardware feasibility: bias-preserving CX gates are forbidden in naturally biased platforms and remain challenging in engineered ones, so the benefits depend on implementing high-fidelity alternative operations.
paper_title: Biased-noise qubits: a guide to efficient fault-tolerance using the hierarchy of errors
